title: High‐solid epoxy coatings incorporating propylene glycol monomethyl ether as a safer alternative to xylene
content:
Abstract

High-solid epoxy coatings have gained increasing attention as environmentally responsible protective coatings because their high solids content can reduce solvent requirements while maintaining good mechanical and corrosion protection properties. This study evaluates the effect of replacing xylene with propylene glycol monomethyl ether (PM) in high-solid epoxy coatings, with particular emphasis on corrosion performance and volatile organic compound (VOC) composition. Corrosion resistance was evaluated using Linear Polarization Resistance (LPR) and weight-loss measurements. The PM-based coating exhibited higher corrosion rates than the xylene-based coating, with values of 2.85 × 10−5 and 8.71 mpy compared with 1.36 × 10−5 and 2.18 mpy, respectively. Nevertheless, both systems exhibited high corrosion inhibition performance under the test conditions. VOC analysis showed that the xylene-based formulation contained detectable ethylbenzene and xylene isomers, whereas these aromatic compounds were not detected in the PM-based formulation. Instead, 1-methoxy-2-propanol was the major identified solvent component in the PM formulation. Although the total measured VOC content increased from 99.15 g/L for the xylene formulation to 120.66 g/L for the PM formulation, the substitution of detectable aromatic hydrocarbons with an oxygenated solvent substantially changed the VOC composition. The novelty of this study lies in demonstrating that PM substitution can modify the VOC hazard profile of a high-solid epoxy coating while maintaining substantial corrosion protection.
